categories.name: Nursery
categories.intro: Safe sleep starts with a firm, empty sleep space. Anchor any dresser to the wall. Skip bumpers, pillows, and quilts in the crib.

categories.name: Sleep
categories.intro: Alone, on the back, on a firm flat mattress, with nothing else in the sleep space. A swaddle or wearable sleep sack is the cover.

categories.name: Clothing
categories.intro: Use the low end of each range if you do laundry every 2–3 days, and the high end if you'd rather do it less. Zip-up sleepers with two-way zippers beat snaps at 3 AM. Skip baby shoes before walking, fancy outfits, and newborn-size jeans.

categories.name: Feeding
categories.intro: If you plan to breastfeed, check insurance before you buy a pump. If you plan to use formula, buy one small can first and talk with your baby's clinician. Don't stock up on one bottle brand until the baby has tried it.

categories.name: Diapering
categories.intro: Newborns outgrow newborn size fast. Start with one or two small packs plus size 1, and keep receipts.

categories.name: Bath
categories.intro: Newborns only need a few baths a week, and sponge baths until the umbilical cord stump falls off. Bath toys can wait.

categories.name: Gear
categories.intro: Most hospitals expect a rear-facing car seat for the ride home. Buy the car seat new, or only use one whose history you trust. Have the install checked.

categories.name: Health and safety
categories.intro: This is a shopping list, not dosing or treatment advice. Ask your pediatrician before using any medicine, including infant acetaminophen.

categories.name: Toys and development
categories.intro: A play mat and a few high-contrast books cover the early months. Big toy hauls before 3 months are easy to skip.

items.name: Crib (meets current safety standards)
items.note: Fixed sides only. No drop-sides. Keep it away from windows, cords, and shelves.
items.ownedNote: Confirm it meets current safety standards and has fixed sides. No drop-side cribs. Replace it if you do not know its history.

items.name: Mini or compact crib
items.note: For a small room, this replaces the full-size crib. It still needs current safety standards, fixed sides, and a firm mattress made for that frame.
items.ownedNote: Same checks as a full crib: current standards, fixed sides, and a known history.

items.name: Firm crib mattress
items.note: Firm and tight-fitting. You should not be able to fit more than two fingers between the mattress and the frame. No extra padding.
items.ownedNote: Buy new unless you know its history. It should be firm and fit the frame tightly.

items.imageAlt: Burt's Bees Baby fitted crib sheet
items.name: Fitted crib sheets (2–3)
items.note: Fitted sheets only. Match them to the mattress size you are actually using.

items.name: Waterproof mattress protector (2)
items.note: Use a protector made for your mattress. Don't add loose pads.

items.name: Dresser + changing topper

picks.budget: IKEA Hemnes/Malm (anchor it to the wall)

items.note: A dresser with a changing topper replaces a standalone changing table. Anchor it to the wall.
items.ownedNote: Anchor it to the wall before a child can climb. Check that drawers stop so they cannot be pulled all the way out onto a child.

items.name: Changing pad + 2 covers
items.note: Use it on a dresser or another stable surface, not as a reason to buy a separate changing table.

items.name: Glider or rocker
items.note: A chair you already find comfortable is enough at first.
items.ownedNote: Check that it is stable and that any recalls have been handled.

items.name: Blackout curtains
items.note: Keep cords out of reach.

items.imageAlt: Yogasleep Dohm Classic white noise machine
items.name: White noise machine
items.note: A free phone app covers the budget option, so you may not need to buy hardware.

items.name: Furniture anchors
items.note: Anchor the dresser and any other furniture that could tip once a child climbs.

items.name: Changing table (standalone)
items.note: Use a dresser topper or a changing pad on a stable surface instead.

items.name: Crib bumpers, pillows, quilts
items.note: These are unsafe in a crib. Leave the sleep space empty.

items.name: Bassinet (first months)
items.note: Useful beside your bed for the first months, including when a nursery is also ready. Use only the mattress made for it.
items.ownedNote: Check the weight limit, recalls, and that the mattress is the one made for that model.

items.name: Swaddles (3–4)

picks.mid: Halo SleepSack Swaddle / Love to Dream

items.note: Try a couple of styles. Babies have opinions. Stop swaddling when the baby shows signs of rolling, and ask your pediatrician if you are unsure.

items.imageAlt: Burt's Bees Baby wearable sleep sack
items.name: Wearable sleep sacks (2–3)
items.note: This is the blanket. Choose a warmer TOG for fall and winter, and a lighter one for spring and summer.

items.imageAlt: Infant Optics DXR-8 video baby monitor
items.name: Video monitor
items.note: Nice-to-have in a small single-level home. Treat it as a must-have if the baby sleeps in another room or you live on more than one level.

items.name: Play yard
items.note: If the baby sleeps here, use only the bassinet or firm mattress made for that model. Don't add extra padding.
items.ownedNote: Check recalls and the weight limit. Use only the mattress made for that model.

items.name: Inclined sleepers, sleep positioners
items.note: These are unsafe for sleep. Skip them.

items.imageAlt: Simple Joys by Carter's newborn sleepers
items.name: Newborn clothing

picks.budget: Simple Joys by Carter's / Cat & Jack

items.note: Some babies skip this size. Keep the tags on. Gifts often cover it.

items.imageAlt: Simple Joys by Carter's 0–3 month sleepers
items.name: 0–3 month clothing

picks.budget: Simple Joys by Carter's / Cat & Jack

items.note: The size they'll wear most at first. Prefer zip-up sleepers with two-way zippers.

items.imageAlt: Simple Joys by Carter's 3–6 month sleepers
items.name: 3–6 month clothing

picks.budget: Simple Joys by Carter's / Cat & Jack

items.note: Buy for the season these months will fall in. Fine to wait for gifts and your shower.

items.name: 6–9 month clothing

picks.budget: Simple Joys by Carter's / Cat & Jack

items.note: Wait. Gifts tend to cover these sizes.

items.name: 9–12 month clothing

picks.budget: Simple Joys by Carter's / Cat & Jack

items.note: Wait. Buy for the season when you get there.

items.name: Baby shoes before walking
items.note: Skip shoes until the baby is walking.

items.name: Fancy outfits
items.note: Photos are nicer in sleepers you will actually use.

items.name: Newborn-size jeans
items.note: Skip these. Soft sleepers and bodysuits are the clothes that get worn.

items.imageAlt: Medela Pump in Style Advanced breast pump
items.name: Breast pump (check insurance first)
items.note: In the U.S., most insurance plans cover a pump. Call before you pay. Ask which models are covered and when you can order.

items.name: Manual pump or silicone collector
items.note: Optional backup for breastfeeding or combo feeding. Not a must-have.

items.name: Nursing bras (2–3)
items.note: Two or three is enough to start.

items.name: Nipple cream
items.note: A common comfort item for breastfeeding. Ask a lactation consultant if feeding is painful.

items.name: Breast pads
items.note: Disposable or reusable. You do not need both piles on day one.

items.name: Milk storage bags
items.note: For milk you plan to store. Buy a modest box first.

items.name: Nursing pillow
items.note: Helpful for positioning. A class or a lactation visit will show you options too.

items.name: Bottles
items.note: Start small. Breastfeeding plans usually need 2–4 small bottles later. Formula plans usually need 6–8. Combo plans usually need 4–6. Don't stock up on one brand until the baby has tried it.

items.name: Bottle brush + drying rack
items.note: You will use this with even a few bottles.

items.name: Formula (one small can first)
items.note: Buy one small can first. Talk with the baby's clinician about formula. Store-brand formulas sold in the U.S. have to meet the same FDA standards.

items.name: Burp cloths (6–10)
items.note: Scatter them where you feed. Six to ten is the useful range.

items.name: Bottle sterilizer or dryer
items.note: Nice-to-have. Hot soapy water or the dishwasher is enough for many families.

items.name: Formula dispenser or pitcher
items.note: Optional if you are formula feeding. A simple pitcher is enough. You do not need a formula-maker machine.

items.name: Formula maker machine
items.note: Most families can skip the machine. A pitcher or a single bottle at a time is enough.

items.imageAlt: Breast pump tote for Spectra and Medela
items.name: Pump bag
items.note: For daycare or work, if you are pumping away from home.

items.name: Second set of pump parts
items.note: Extra flanges and bottles so one set can be in the wash while the other is at daycare.

items.name: High chair (around 6 months)
items.note: Wait until you are closer to starting solids, around 6 months.

items.name: Diapers (small newborn pack, then size 1)
items.note: One or two newborn packs, then size 1. Keep receipts so you can swap sizes.

items.name: Wipes
items.note: Sensitive wipes are the usual starting point.

items.name: Diaper cream
items.note: One tube is enough to start.

items.name: Diaper pail or lidded trash can
items.note: A lidded can you already own is a fair budget option.

items.imageAlt: Skip Hop Forma diaper bag backpack
items.name: Diaper bag
items.note: A backpack you already like can be the bag.

items.imageAlt: Skip Hop Pronto portable changing pad
items.name: Portable changing pad
items.note: Often included with the diaper bag.

items.name: Wipe warmer
items.note: Most parents say skip it.

items.name: Second diaper station (caddy + pad)
items.note: For a multi-level home. Keep diapers, wipes, and cream within arm's reach on each floor you use.

items.name: Bottle labels
items.note: For daycare or a sitter. Label bottles and anything you send.

items.name: Cooler bag
items.note: For milk or formula bottles that travel to daycare.

items.name: Infant tub
items.note: Sponge baths come first, until the cord stump falls off.

items.imageAlt: Cetaphil baby shampoo and body wash
items.name: Gentle wash
items.note: One gentle wash is enough.

items.name: Hooded towels (2–3) + washcloths
items.note: Two or three towels plus a few washcloths.

items.imageAlt: Frida Baby NailFrida infant nail clipper
items.name: Nail clippers or file
items.note: A manual clipper or file is enough.

items.name: Bath thermometer
items.note: Nice-to-have. Test the water on your wrist either way.

items.name: Bath toys (before 6 months)
items.note: Skip toys for the early months. They are hard to dry and easy to add later.

items.imageAlt: Chicco KeyFit 30 infant car seat and base
items.name: Infant car seat (buy new)
items.note: Buy this new unless you know its full history. Most hospitals expect a rear-facing seat for the ride home, including families who mostly walk or take transit. Have the install checked.
items.ownedNote: Check the expiration date, recall list, and that no parts are missing. Replace it if you do not know its history, including whether it has been in a crash.

items.imageAlt: Baby Jogger City Mini GT2 travel system
items.name: Stroller

picks.mid: Baby Jogger City Mini / City Select

items.note: A travel system that accepts your infant car seat covers most families. Check that it fits in your trunk and that you can fold it one-handed.
items.ownedNote: Check recalls, the brake, the harness, and that the fold still locks.

items.name: Carrier or wrap
items.note: Must-have if you mostly walk, use transit, or mix walking and driving. Otherwise nice-to-have.
items.ownedNote: Check recalls and that buckles, rings, and seams are intact.

items.name: Bouncer
items.note: A supervised awake spot only. Not a sleep space.

items.name: Compact travel stroller
items.note: Add one if you fly often. Many families wait and use their main stroller first.
items.ownedNote: Check recalls, the brake, and the fold lock.

items.name: Electric swing
items.note: Nice-to-have. Use it awake and supervised. Not a sleep space.

items.name: Car mirror
items.note: Nice-to-have. It does not replace a correct install.

items.imageAlt: Skip Hop winter car seat cover
items.name: Car-seat-safe cover
items.note: For fall and winter. Use a cover that goes over the seat, not a bulky snowsuit under the harness. Bulky layers can keep the harness from fitting snugly.

items.imageAlt: Stroller sun shade and mosquito net
items.name: Stroller sun shade
items.note: For spring and summer. Sunscreen isn't recommended before 6 months, so stick to shade and clothing.

items.name: Fan
items.note: For spring and summer air circulation. Do not aim it directly at the baby, and do not add loose bedding.

items.name: Digital thermometer (rectal for newborns)
items.note: Rectal readings are the usual reference for newborns. Ask your pediatrician to show you before you need it at 2 AM. This page does not give medical instructions.

items.name: Nasal aspirator
items.note: A bulb syringe is the simple version.

items.name: Saline drops
items.note: Named with the thermometer and nasal aspirator in the health kit about 8 weeks before the due date. Ask your pediatrician which product to use.

items.imageAlt: Infants' Tylenol pain and fever reliever
items.name: Infant acetaminophen
items.note: Ask your pediatrician about whether to use it and about dosing before you ever give it. This site does not list doses.

items.name: Cool-mist humidifier
items.note: Nice-to-have in warm months. Treat it as a must-have in fall and winter. Clean it on the schedule in its manual.

items.name: Baby gates (by about 6 months)
items.note: Wait until you are closer to crawling. A multi-level home should plan on a second set.

items.name: Outlet covers, cabinet locks
items.note: Wait until crawling is close. Do it before the baby is mobile, not before the birth.

items.name: Smoke and CO detectors checked
items.note: Test the detectors you already have. Replace any that are missing, expired, or silent. This is a task, not a branded product.

items.name: Baby first aid kit
items.note: Nice-to-have. Your pediatrician's after-hours number matters more than the kit.

items.name: Play mat or gym
items.note: Useful once tummy time is part of the day. Not needed for the hospital bag.

items.name: High-contrast cards or board books
items.note: A cheap must-have. The library and black-and-white printables count.

items.name: Soft rattles and teethers (3+ months)
items.note: Wait until about 3 months. You do not need a basket of them.

items.name: Activity center (5+ months)
items.note: Wait. This is a mid-first-year item, not a newborn one.

items.name: Big toy hauls before 3 months
items.note: Skip the haul. A play mat and a few high-contrast books are plenty.
